column1: # TIER-2 HELD-OUT CASES. EMPTY ON PURPOSE, created 2026-10-23.
# THE ONE RULE: no threshold decision may consult this file until the thresholds
# are final. Not "should not" -- the point of a held-out set is that it is spent
# the first time it is read. docs/validation-cases.tsv is the development set and
# is where tuning happens; a matrix from that file is in-sample and
# scripts/holdout.py prices what the tuning bought
# Same columns and same bar as the development set: a paper, erratum or redesign
# reporting how an assay ALREADY IN THE REGISTRY performed, with `as_of` no later
# than the sequences its authors could have seen. A new assay's validation
# against its own panel does not qualify -- it says nothing about drift.
# Target: 15-20 cases, at least 5 with `mechanism: drift`. The development set
# has exactly one drift-mechanism case against ten coverage cases, so the drift
# flag currently has one ground-truth event; that is the gap to close first.
# docs/journal/2026-10-06-lab-leads.md. Read each paper once for both this and the C2

column1: # ROWS ADDED 2026-10-24 by a literature sweep over the 200 live registry entries
# (three passes, one per third of the registry; see docs/journal/2026-10-24-heldout-candidates.md
# for the leads that did NOT clear the bar and for every assay searched without result).
# Each row was accepted only where the full text was read AND the assay identity was
# confirmed by printed primer names or sequences. Independence is NOT assumed: a row
# whose assay already has a development-set row says NOT INDEPENDENT, and rows from one
# paper and one experiment say ONE EVENT, so nobody counts 30 rows as 30 events.

column5: 10.1128/jcm.02505-21 Geiselhardt 2022: Table 1 prints CDV4.1-F/CDV3-R/CD3.1-FAMas as CDV-Mix 3, all three exact to the registry. Alignment found mismatches in the forward primer and probe; in triplicate the authors' new set was significantly more sensitive on Asia-4 and was the only assay giving positive Cq for PDV. Mechanism read as coverage, not drift: the Asia-4 strains used (MH496772/MH496775) were deposited in 2018, before this 2021 design. ONE EVENT with the Mix7 row below (same paper, same experiment).

10.1128/jcm.02505-21 Geiselhardt 2022: Table 1 prints CDV-1808-F/CDV-1903-R/CDV-1842-FAM as CDV-Mix 7, exact to the registry. Mismatches in the reverse primer and probe; the new set was significantly more sensitive on Asia-4 and Mix 7 gave no PDV signal. Mix 7 was best on Europe-1 FFPE and the America-1 vaccine strain, so the failure is genotype-specific. ONE EVENT with the Mix3 row above.

10.1186/s40794-020-00114-2 Fieldhouse 2020: Table 1 prints polFouter/polRouter byte-identical to the registry, cited to Wellehan 2004. On 599 nasopharyngeal swabs (Sarawak, 2017-18) the nested pol PCR gave 74 positives against 62 for a real-time AdV assay; sequencing recovered HAdV-7 and, in two patients, Desmodus rotundus adenovirus 1 at 100% identity to KX774303. NOT INDEPENDENT: this assay already has a development-set row. ONE EVENT with round2.

10.1186/s40794-020-00114-2 Fieldhouse 2020: Table 1 prints polFinner/polRinner byte-identical to the registry. The 74-of-599 figure is the nested read-out, so round 2 produced the sequenced amplicons. Caveat: a separate hexon nested PCR (Lu & Erdman 2006, not a registry entry) found 84 of 428 on its own subset, so the pol assay did not reach every hexon-positive specimen. ONE EVENT with round1.

10.1002/jmv.70389 Habeebur-Rahman 2025: Table 1 prints CoV-FWD1/CoV-RVS1 as the Quan assay; the reverse is exact and the forward identical with inosine where the registry stores N. On 346 bat faecal samples from 29 species this assay found 50 positives and a Watanabe-derived assay 44, only 18 shared (kappa 0.286), so each missed about 30 the other found. NOT INDEPENDENT: assay already in the development set. ONE EVENT with round2.

10.1002/jmv.70389 Habeebur-Rahman 2025: Table 1 prints CoV-FWD2/CoV-RVS2 byte-identical to the registry. The 50-of-346 count is the nested round-2 read-out; 26 samples called positive by the other assay were negative through the full nested protocol. Positives spanned six subgenus-level clades. NOT INDEPENDENT: assay already in the development set. ONE EVENT with round1.

10.3389/fvets.2022.924854 Galvin 2022: Methods print vAAPV-124f, vAAPV-246r and the vAAPV-159 MGB probe, all three exact to the registry, following Baek 2020. Applied to 554 hummingbird carcasses across four taxa and 1,050 live birds: 20% of carcasses positive (Anna's 30%, Allen's 13%, Selasphorus 5%, Black-chinned 1%) and 32.5% of live-caught birds, against 1.5% by visual lesion scoring of 13,542 banded birds. Amplified from birds with no visible lesions.

10.3390/v15122327 Song 2023: in-silico evaluation of 18 MPXV assays against 5,210 NCBI genomes; the N3R set is attributed to the registry's own design DOI and the printed oligo lengths match. N3R gave 72 perfect alignments, 4,695 partial (predominant defect at probe position 12) and 443 outright mismatches. MECHANISM IS AN INFERENCE, not the paper's word: 5,043 of the genomes are post-2022 Clade IIb B lineages, so the matching slice is largely pre-outbreak. ONE EVENT with the F3L row.

10.3390/v15122327 Song 2023: the F3L set attributed to Kulesh 2004 gave 51 perfect alignments of 5,210 genomes, 5,146 partial with the predominant mismatch at the reverse primer's first base, and 13 outright mismatches. A 5'-terminal mismatch is the mildest kind, so this is mismatch-present rather than detection-failure. Mechanism inferred as above. ONE EVENT with the N3R row. Corroborated but not independently by 10.2807/1560-7917.ES.2022.27.32.2200497 Huggett 2022, which flags the same two positions.

10.3390/v15122327 Song 2023: the ATI conventional-PCR set is attributed to the registry's design DOI and the printed primer lengths (16 and 18 nt) and GC match. Zero perfect alignments across all 5,210 genomes: 5,190 partial with the predominant mismatch at the reverse primer's first base, 20 outright mismatches, 14 alignments carrying ambiguous bases. Coverage rather than drift precisely because not even Clade I genomes align perfectly, which cannot be post-2022 change.

10.1371/journal.pone.0058372 Fischer 2013: a 16-laboratory ring trial in which the original Vazquez-Moron 2006 protocol was run by its own designer (a co-author). Variations of the pan-lyssavirus assays detected almost every RABV and EBLV isolate, but the original protocol generally failed to recognise the Nigerian sample L-15 (RABV clade Africa 2, dog brain, 1989) and returned a doubtful result at the 1e-3 dilution of isolate 20293. Table 4 scores every method against every panel sample. Applies at protocol level, so round2 is the same event.

10.1186/s12985-023-01972-w Vanmechelen 2023: Table 1 prints FAP59 and FAP64 identical to the registry, cited to Forslund 1999. Two novel papillomavirus genomes from a captive North American porcupine were recovered by rolling-circle amplification; of five degenerate primer pairs tried, all failed to amplify, and specific primers had to be built from FAP59/FAP64 with every degenerate site replaced by the target's own base. NOT INDEPENDENT: this assay already has a development-set row (its own bench panel).

10.3390/v16101558 Matias 2024: Table 1 prints FAP59/FAP64 identical to the registry, cited to Forslund 1999. In a bovine oesophageal carcinoma-in-situ lesion the FAP amplicon sequenced as BPV2 alone (99.78% to KF284153) while rolling-circle amplification plus high-throughput sequencing of the same lesion recovered BPV2 complete plus BPV4 subgenomic fragments, i.e. part of the diversity present. FAP did amplify where MY09/MY11 did not. Independent of the Vanmechelen row (different host, genus, year).

10.3390/v16050805 Villanueva 2024: Methods print reverse BornaPCA6 and probe BornaP_Fam character-for-character as the registry stores them, cited to Sigrist 2021. Of 124 captive psittacines in Taiwan, 57 were positive (45.97%), products gel-confirmed and three brain samples sequenced on the X/P gene, resolving PaBV-2 and PaBV-4. IDENTITY CAVEAT RESOLVED 2026-10-24, it was a false alarm: GATCCGCAGACAGYACGT is the registry's own alternate forward BornaPCA3A, stored on this entry beside the primary BornaPCA3 CCCGCAGACAGYACGT. Sigrist 2021 section 2.2 says the design has "two variants of a degenerate forward primer and a single degenerate reverse primer", so the registry holding two forwards is the paper's own design and Villanueva simply used the second variant. Same assay, no trim, nothing to reconcile.

10.3201/eid2003.131557 Groch 2014 (publication date; no received date available): Methods print both registry oligos exactly. The universal morbillivirus P-gene pair amplified a 374 bp fragment from the lung of a stranded Guiana dolphin, and the amplicon (KF711855) placed the strain in the CeMV clade but distinct from described dolphin morbillivirus, i.e. the 1993 primers still detected a previously undescribed cetacean morbillivirus. The sibling entry Morbillivirus_including_CDV_P_gene_Barrett_2003 stores the same pair, so it is the same event.

10.1186/s12936-021-04019-z Harl 2022: prints HaemNFI and HaemNR3 verbatim, identical to the registry. States the nested assay does not allow amplification of the cytB of parasites of the Leucocytozoon toddi group; HaemNFI carries a 2 bp 3' mismatch and HaemR2 four mismatches to the H. elani/hBUBT1 group. 60 of 183 raptors carried toddi-group lineages recoverable only with other primers. NOT INDEPENDENT: this assay already has a development-set row (Lotta 2019). ONE EVENT with the Pan_Plasmodium row.

10.1186/s12936-021-04019-z Harl 2022: prints HaemF and HaemR2 verbatim, identical to the registry. Same finding: the second-round Leucocytozoon primers miss the toddi group, and the raptor lineages were recovered only with other primers. ONE EVENT with the Pan_hemoparasite row above.

10.1186/s12985-021-01694-x Lee 2021: primer table prints DFA and KG1 exactly as the registry stores them. In three wild-born Bornean elephant calves with fatal EEHV haemorrhagic disease, confirmed EEHV1A by a specific assay, the consensus polymerase and terminase PCRs did not detect herpesvirus in any tested sample. NOT INDEPENDENT: this assay already has a development-set row. ONE EVENT with the three sibling rows and the two pan-EEHV works rows below (same paper, same samples).
10.1186/s12985-021-01694-x Lee 2021: the table prints TGV and IYG exactly as the registry stores them. Same experiment and same negative result for the nested round. ONE EVENT with the sibling rows.

10.1186/s12985-021-01694-x Lee 2021: the table prints the terminase round-1 pair in deoxyinosine-substituted form of the registry's sequences, and again under their LGH names. Same experiment and same negative result. ONE EVENT with the sibling rows.
10.1186/s12985-021-01694-x Lee 2021: the table prints the terminase round-2 pair matching the registry. Same experiment and same negative result. ONE EVENT with the sibling rows.

10.1186/s12985-021-01694-x Lee 2021: primer table prints 6711/6710 exactly as the registry stores them. This is the assay that made the diagnosis the consensus assays missed, sequence-confirmed as EEHV1A (OK635292, OK635293). The works and fails rows from this paper are the same event, and that pairing is the point: a specific assay found what the pan-family assay did not.
10.1186/s12985-021-01694-x Lee 2021: the table prints 6712 with 6710 for round 2A, exact to the registry, and Table 4 is titled as the cleaned sequences of that round. ONE EVENT with the round-1 row.

10.3390/v14020411 Yang 2022: Appendix A prints primers 7400 and 6719 with Latimer's own numbering, exact to the registry. Screen of 281 Asian elephants in China (126 wild, 155 captive) yielding 11 EEHV4 detections. ONE EVENT with the three sibling EEHV rows from this paper.

10.3390/v14020411 Yang 2022: Appendix A prints 6720 with 6719, exact to the registry; the inner round of the same semi-nested assay that produced the EEHV4 detections. ONE EVENT with the sibling rows.

10.3390/v14020411 Yang 2022: Appendix A prints 7484 and 7483, exact to the registry. EEHV5 was found in one captive elephant (trunk and oral swabs) of the 281 screened, so this is a thin positive. ONE EVENT with the sibling rows.
10.3390/v14020411 Yang 2022: Appendix A prints 7424 with 7484, exact to the registry, as the inner round of the same EEHV5 assay. ONE EVENT with the sibling rows.

10.1038/s42003-024-06092-x Blanvillain 2024: names the registry primer Oo-rt-ITS-R with ITS3 and cites the registry's own design DOI. 109 of 1,254 European snakes positive, with positives spanning both clade I and clade II of the pathogen. NOT INDEPENDENT: this assay already has a development-set row, and the registry currently reads insufficient data on 7 evaluable records, so this row is informative about the data gap as much as the assay.

10.3389/fmicb.2024.1504621 Harhay 2025: Table 2 prints INVA-F and INVA-R exact to both registry oligos and cites Rahn 1992 for them. Run as one target of an 8-plex on 1,303 Salmonella isolates, invA failed to amplify in 3 (serovars Anatum, Eko, Kentucky). NOT INDEPENDENT: this assay already has a development-set works row (Malorny 2003). A 3-in-1,303 failure rate is a weak signal and the row should be read that way.

10.1371/journal.pone.0344743 Supradhnya Namdeo 2026: Table 1 prints ME1 and ME2 with the registry's primer names, exact sequences and 250 bp amplicon. Used as the reference standard against a new latex agglutination test, with 151 of 194 field samples positive. Worth having because the registry entry itself was accepted on thin in-silico evidence.

10.3390/ani16193112 Otero Soberon 2026: Methods print MDS-400 and MDS-402 character-for-character as the registry stores them (MDS-402 is the registry forward). 18 of 28 Peruvian snakes positive, across 6 of 7 taxa sampled.

column1: # ROWS ADDED 2026-10-24 (late) from the Usutu lead that docs/journal/2026-10-24-heldout-candidates.md called the
# cheapest unexplored win. Method was the one that doc recommends: paste each stored oligo into Europe PMC
# full-text search in quotes. It also returned Joest 2011 ITSELF, so the entry's oligos are now verified
# verbatim against their own design paper, the 21 nt reverse included.

column5: 10.1371/journal.pone.0032604 Becker 2012 (Epizootic emergence of Usutu virus in wild and captive birds in Germany): a literal Europe PMC full-text search on all three stored oligos returns this paper, so identity is the sequences themselves and not a primer name. Of 223 dead birds collected from June 2011, USUV RNA was detected by this real-time RT-PCR in 86 birds across 6 species, and the detection is ORTHOGONALLY CONFIRMED three ways: virus isolated in cell culture from the heart of 18 blackbirds, USUV antigen shown by immunohistochemistry in brain, heart, liver and lung, and the complete polyprotein coding sequence obtained by deep sequencing. That triple confirmation is what makes this a real `works` row rather than a count of Ct values. ONE EVENT with the 2012 German outbreak.

10.3390/v16010079 Hars/Lecollinet 2024 (Evaluation of non-vector transmission of Usutu virus in domestic canaries): prints the stored probe and reverse, found by literal full-text search on the oligos. Canaries were experimentally challenged intranasally and this assay detected systemic dissemination of USUV above a 10^2 TCID50 dose and oronasal excretion of infectious particles, with infectivity confirmed independently by titration in cell culture. The value of this row is its DATE: a 2011 assay still detecting virus in 2024, which is the direct test of this entry's own primer_site_polymorphic flag. Experimental challenge rather than field surveillance, so it prices sensitivity on known-positive material, not lineage coverage.

10.1186/s13071-025-06841-9 Schmidt 2025 (louse flies, Germany): 1 of 1000 louse flies USUV-positive, an Ornithomya avicularia taken from a European Robin in Saxony in July 2020. WEAKEST OF THE THREE AND KEPT AS SUCH, for two stated reasons. The authors could not sequence the USUV-positive sample -- their own words, it "did not contain enough viral RNA" -- so unlike their SINV positive this detection has no orthogonal confirmation. And IDENTITY IS NOT EXACT: their Table 1 prints the reverse as GCTAGTAGTTCTTATGGA, 18 nt, where the registry and Joest 2011 both print GCTAGTAGTAGTTCTTATGGA, 21 nt, and their stated fragment is 88 bp against the registry's measured 91 -- a difference of exactly the three missing bases, so it is internally consistent and is their trim rather than a slip in one number. The forward and probe are identical.
